evals.name: Windows Server 2022 — pktmon HTTP capture
evals.prompt: Capture HTTP traffic on a Windows Server 2022 box without installing Wireshark. I need to see the full payload.
evals.context: Server 2022 is fully patched. WinRM is enabled. You have local admin access. No Wireshark or third-party tools installed on the server.
expectations: Recommends pktmon (not netsh trace) because the target is Server 2022 (pktmon in-box since Server 2019)
Instructs adding a pktmon filter for port 80 before starting the capture
Uses --pkt-size 0 flag to capture full packet payloads (not the default 128-byte truncation)
Converts the ETL output using 'pktmon etl2pcap' on the server or laptop
Includes a step to copy the pcapng file to the analyst laptop for Wireshark analysis
Mentions the authorization/safety gate: confirm you are authorized to capture on this host before starting

evals.name: Windows Server 2016 — netsh trace fallback
evals.prompt: Same task: capture HTTP traffic on a Windows Server 2016 box without installing Wireshark.
evals.context: Server 2016 is fully patched. WinRM is enabled. You have local admin access. No Wireshark or third-party tools installed on the server.
expectations: Recognizes that pktmon is NOT available on Server 2016 and falls back to netsh trace
Uses 'netsh trace start capture=yes report=disabled' with appropriate flags
Adds an optional capture filter (e.g. IPv4.Address or TCP.Port) to scope the trace
Advises stopping with 'netsh trace stop' and retrieving only the .etl file (not the .cab)
Instructs converting the ETL to pcapng on the analyst laptop using etl2pcapng.exe (not on the server)
References the etl2pcapng GitHub release for the binary

evals.name: ESXi uplink capture with pktcap-uw
evals.prompt: I need to see all traffic on an ESXi host's uplink (physical NIC). The host is managed by vCenter. Show me how to capture without installing anything extra.
evals.context: ESXi 8.0 host. SSH is currently disabled (default). You have root credentials. A datastore is available for writing capture files.
expectations: Instructs enabling SSH on the ESXi host before starting (via vSphere Client, DCUI, or vim-cmd hostsvc/enable_ssh)
Uses 'net-stats -l' or equivalent to identify the correct uplink port number and vmnic name
Uses pktcap-uw --uplink <vmnicX> with UplinkSndKernel,UplinkRcvKernel (no spaces in the capture list)
Includes -s 0 for full snaplen and -c <count> to bound the capture
Writes output to a real datastore path (not the ESXi ramdisk)
Provides the kill recipe (lsof | grep pktcap-uw or pkill pktcap-uw) to stop a runaway capture
Mentions the option to live-pipe to Wireshark via SSH as a community pattern (not officially documented)

evals.name: vCenter appliance (VCSA) — tcpdump on Photon OS
evals.prompt: I need to capture packets on the vCenter Server Appliance management NIC to debug a connectivity issue between vCenter and an ESXi host.
evals.context: VCSA 8.0 (Photon OS). SSH is currently disabled. You have root credentials via VAMI. The analyst laptop has Wireshark installed.
expectations: Recommends tcpdump (not pktcap-uw, which is ESXi-only and not present on VCSA)
Instructs enabling SSH via VAMI https://<VCSA>:5480 or using 'ssh.set --enabled true' in appliancesh
Notes that SSH lands in restricted appliancesh and user must type 'shell' to get a bash prompt
Uses 'tcpdump -i eth0 -s 0 -w /tmp/<filename>.pcap' with a BPF filter to bound the capture
Includes 'not port 22' in the filter when running a live pipe to avoid capturing the SSH control session
Shows how to copy the file to the laptop with scp
Mentions Wireshark sshdump extcap as an alternative to the manual SSH pipe
Reminds user to disable SSH on VCSA when the capture is complete

evals.name: Meraki — east-west capture on MS switch (same VLAN)
evals.prompt: Two clients on the same VLAN behind a Meraki MS switch can't talk to each other. I need to capture their traffic to debug it.
evals.context: Meraki MS switch managed via Dashboard. There is also an MX security appliance as the upstream router. Both clients are on the same VLAN and subnet.
expectations: Recommends capturing at the MS switch (not the MX), because the MX cannot see LAN-to-LAN switched traffic
Directs the user to Dashboard Network-wide > Monitor > Packet capture, selecting the MS and relevant interface
Specifies setting Output to 'Download .pcap file (for Wireshark)' rather than the live browser stream
Alternatively suggests configuring a SPAN / port mirror on the MS: Switch > Monitor > Switch ports > Mirror
Explicitly notes the fidelity caveat: Dashboard captures are not guaranteed 100% under load
Notes that live-streaming to Wireshark is not officially supported via Dashboard
